question: Should OpenClaw adopt one ordered, channel-agnostic sender-authentication-strength contract for ingress authorization, beginning with the three proposed levels and an opt-in `verified` threshold?
rationale: The RFC changes the long-term security and compatibility contract shared by channel adapters and the ingress authorization gate; source review alone cannot determine the acceptable cross-channel semantics or upgrade policy.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped RFC discussion
options.body: Accept the three-level direction for discussion, require per-channel classification evidence, and stop before implementation if any bundled channel lacks a defensible mapping.

options.title: Request a narrower design
options.body: Keep the security goal but constrain the RFC to a specific channel family or a more limited policy contract before considering shared ingress changes.

options.title: Decline shared core abstraction
options.body: Leave channel-specific trust handling outside the common ingress contract and document why a universal ordering is not supportable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped RFC discussion
recommendation.body: Accept the three-level direction for discussion, require per-channel classification evidence, and stop before implementation if any bundled channel lacks a defensible mapping.

likelyOwner.reason: The author has supplied the concrete security rationale and requested the two central design decisions; broader core ownership needs confirmation from maintainers during discussion.
